transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining the weekly carve-out review. As we discussed, the company is transferring its analytics division to the buyer next month, and that division relies on a third-party software platform. The current assignment draft transfers our software rights to the buyer at closing. The software vendor has been informed of the transaction but has not yet signed the assignment document. Before I approve the assignment package, I need IP counsel and carve-out counsel to identify any required conditions and operational protections we should have in place. What are we missing?

transcript.text: I confirmed with the division's operations lead yesterday that the buyer needs uninterrupted access to the platform for exactly 120 days after closing while its replacement system is configured. That operational requirement has not yet been added to the transition schedule, and we need to address it before the assignment package is approved.

transcript.text: Elena, before we go further on the assignment package, I need to flag something I found in the vendor's legacy contract archive. The original license agreement contains an anti-assignment clause that requires the vendor's prior written consent to any assignment, and critically, that consent must specifically name the buyer as the permitted successor. This clause was omitted from the circulated contract abstract, so it hasn't been reflected in the approval materials or the assignment draft yet. Until we obtain a signed consent from the vendor that names the buyer as the permitted successor, the assignment as currently drafted won't be effective under the license terms.
